question.text: A galvanometer having a resistance of $20 \Omega$ and 30 division on both sides has figure of merit 0.005 ampere/ division. The resistance that should be connected in series such that it can be used as a voltmeter upto 15 volt, is:

solution.text:
Deflection current

$=\operatorname{Ig}_{\max }=n x k=0.005 \times 30$

Where, $\mathrm{n}=$ Number of divisions $=30$ and $\mathrm{k}=0.005 \mathrm{amp} /$

division

$\begin{array}{l}

=15 \times 10^{-2}=0.15 \\

\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}[20+\mathrm{R}] \\

15=0.15[20+\mathrm{R}] \\

100=20+\mathrm{R} \\

\mathrm{R}=80 \Omega

\end{array}$
